svg.aria-label: Each core has its own MMU, TLB and L1 cache. All cores share one L2 cache, the DRAM, one copy of the kernel SW, the page table, the COT and one LZ4 HW. Shared tables and the job ring are guarded by locks.
svg.text: Processor and compression layer: what is per core, what is shared

Platform assumptions: P1 no hardware page table walk · P2 per-core L1, one shared L2 · P3 one TLB per core, shared by its threads · P4 LZ4 HW takes N jobs at once. The number of cores and threads is illustrative.
PROCESSOR: several cores, several hardware threads per core
one per core, shared by both threads (P3)
no HW page walk (P1): miss → exception

L2 cache: ONE, shared by all cores (P2)
sees physical addresses only · kernel tables and user SW data compete for it
VA → PA, then L1, L2, DRAM.
2 TLB miss, page is in a frame: the thread that
missed enters kernel SW, which reads the page
table and refills its core's TLB.
3 TLB miss, page is compressed: kernel takes
mm_lock, reads the COT, takes a frame; LZ4 HW
N engines, up to N jobs at once (P4)
· a free engine takes the next job
· completions in finish order, found by tag
· reads and writes DRAM with PAs,
ring_lock before a job is queued
Shared by every core. N is not decided.
Job N+1 waits in the ring for a free engine.
DRAM, 512 MiB of physical address space (widths not to scale)
kernel reads it on a TLB miss
One instance at a time inside.
mm_lock is the one lock over
every table. It is held for table
where a user SW TLB entry points
filled = holds a page, empty = free frame
every kernel SW instance runs the one copy of the code
kernel SW: one copy, an instance per trapping thread
TLBs are private copies of the page table and hardware does not keep them coherent. Before a frame is reused or compressed, the kernel removes that page from the TLB of every core.
Up to one kernel SW instance per hardware thread can run at the same time. They meet only at the locks and at the LZ4 HW, which runs up to N jobs at once.
